body.html: First, let's be clear on one thing: Live n' Leaf Lifestyle Homestay and Cafe is not a "hotel" in the usual sense · It's a small boutique homestay with just 5 rooms and a cafe woven into the house, sitting on Samlan Road in Chiang Mai's Old City near Suan Prung Gate and Chiang Mai Gate · The main thing that sets it apart from ordinary places to stay is its "leaf" theme — green and white with leaf patterns throughout the house, from the room names to the wall art to the furniture and decor · Plenty of real reviews say the same thing: the moment you step inside, you feel relaxed and easy on the eyes, because the whole house feels fresh, like staying in a little garden in the middle of the city · This is a place for people who want a warm, friendly feel rather than the polish of a chain hotel

Who is it for? · Going by real reviews, the people who love Live n' Leaf most are couples or pairs of travelers who want a quiet, fuss-free stay in the Old City · solo travelers who like small places with a host on hand to look after them and give tips · cafe lovers and photo-takers who like a cute, well-designed place with photogenic corners · and people who come to visit the temples and the Sunday Walking Street and want their stay within real walking distance · On the flip side, this place is not for anyone who wants big-resort facilities, because there's no pool, no fitness room, no on-site spa, and very few rooms · If you're traveling as a large family or want 5-star hotel service, this may not be the answer — but if you're after a warm home in the Old City at an affordable price, it does that job well

Location and getting around is where Live n' Leaf has its biggest edge · The property sits on Samlan Road in Phra Singh subdistrict, inside the old city walls of Chiang Mai, near Suan Prung Gate to the southwest and Chiang Mai Gate to the south · From here you can walk to Wat Phra Singh Woramahawihan, a major temple at the center of the Old City, in just a few minutes · The Three Kings Monument and Wat Chedi Luang are also an easy walk away · Best of all, every Sunday night Ratchadamnoen Road turns into the Sunday Walking Street, which is very close — you can walk straight out without hailing a ride · The Chiang Mai Gate market, with its local food and night-time snacks, is also within walking distance · Chiang Mai Airport is only about 2–3 km away, around a 10 min drive, which is very close for a place in the Old City

Rooms and decor · There are only 5 rooms in total, and each one is designed differently, playing with the leaf-and-greenery theme in its own way, so every room has its own charm · The thing real reviews mention most is how clean the rooms are and how comfortable the beds are — many say they woke up feeling fully rested · Every room is air-conditioned with a private bathroom, a fridge, a flat-screen TV, and free Wi-Fi · Some rooms have a balcony or a private sitting area to step out and catch the cool breeze in the morning or evening · The decor leans on cute and easy-on-the-eyes greens and whites with leaf-pattern art, which makes the rooms feel fresh and photograph well — something the social-media crowd loves · One thing to understand is that because this is an old house converted into a homestay, the room size and soundproofing may not match a brand-new hotel, but overall the cleanliness and attention to detail earn praise from nearly everyone

"Waking up in a room decorated with green leaf patterns, heading down for a local-style breakfast at the cafe, then walking straight out to Wat Phra Singh — the location and atmosphere are just right for exploring the Old City."

The cafe and breakfast are another thing that sets Live n' Leaf apart from a typical homestay · Its full name even includes the word "Cafe," because the ground floor is a small cafe decorated with the leaf-and-greenery theme, with a comfortable, sit-and-stay feel · Every morning the property serves a free local-style breakfast from about 8:00 to 10:30 AM, which many guests praise, because you get to try genuine Northern Thai food in a warm, homey setting rather than a standard hotel buffet · Sipping a coffee or a drink in the cafe before heading out to explore, or coming back to relax after a full day of walking, is part of what makes the place feel like a home rather than just a bed · Real reviews say the cafe is quiet and peaceful, good for working or reading, since the neighborhood doesn't have many loud bars to disturb you

Facilities · To be straight about it, Live n' Leaf keeps things simple in true homestay fashion — there's no pool, no fitness room, and no on-site spa · But what it does have is genuinely useful and matches what Old City travelers want · There's bicycle rental for riding around the Old City, which is a way to explore Chiang Mai that a lot of people enjoy · There's a convenient airport transfer, helped by how close the airport is · There's a tour desk / travel advisor to help book Doi Suthep tours, elephant tours, and other activities · There's a balcony, a small garden, parking, a small minimart, and daily housekeeping · There's free Wi-Fi in all rooms · Overall the facilities are fitting for a small homestay, geared toward getting guests out to live in the Old City rather than cooping themselves up at the property

On service · Because it's a homestay run with a close personal touch, it feels more like staying at a friend's or a relative's place than checking into a hotel · Nearly every real review praises the friendliness and helpfulness of the staff and host, who are happy to help book tours, recommend local restaurants, point out walking routes to the temples, and make travel easier · Many say they felt reassured having someone on hand to answer questions and help plan their trips — an upside that big hotels with lots of guests often can't match to the same degree · With only 5 rooms, the staff can look after every guest thoroughly · This is what keeps the property's service review scores consistently high

Atmosphere and quiet · Even though it's in a tourist part of the Old City, Samlan Road and the surrounding lanes are fairly quiet, without many loud bars or nightlife · Many real reviews praise the calm you get from a stay tucked in a lane, while still being able to walk out to the sights in just a few minutes · By day the setting is shady with trees and the property's leaf theme; by night it's quiet enough for a good sleep · For anyone who has stayed around Nimman or near the night market and run into noise problems, this is a choice that offers both quiet and easy access to walking around — a balance that isn't easy to find in Chiang Mai's Old City

Real reviews — the praise · What gets praised most is the Old City location that really does let you walk to the temples and the Walking Street, followed by the cleanliness of the rooms and the comfortable beds · the cute green-and-white leaf decor that photographs well · the friendliness and helpfulness of the host and staff · the local-style breakfast with genuine flavors · and the quiet, comfortable cafe atmosphere · Many sum it up as a warm, homey feel at a price that's worth it for a central Old City location, which is why a number of guests make a point of coming back to stay again

Real reviews — the things to note · One point that comes up is the very small number of rooms (just 5), which means it fills up fast during high season or long weekends, so you need to book ahead · Because it's a house converted into a homestay, the soundproofing between rooms and the size of some rooms may not match a brand-new hotel · There are no resort-style facilities like a pool or fitness room · Some reviews note that parking is limited because it's in an Old City lane · And since it's in the Old City zone, driving in and out during the Sunday Walking Street can be tricky because of road closures · All of this is the kind of thing you can "see coming" for a small homestay in the Old City, rather than serious flaws

Compared with other places in Chiang Mai's Old City · Putting Live n' Leaf next to the popular places in the Old City makes its position clearer · Luxury boutique hotels like Rachamankha or Tamarind Village offer Lanna-style luxury and full service, but cost several times more · A mid-size hotel like De Lanna Hotel offers standard hotel rooms with a pool at a moderate price · Budget hostels and guesthouses offer a cheap bed but lack privacy and design · What Live n' Leaf gives you — and what's hard to find elsewhere at the same price — is a stay in a cute, well-designed house with only 5 rooms, the privacy and close personal care of a homestay, plus a cafe and local-style breakfast, in a location you can walk from · Anyone who wants more than a hostel but isn't ready to pay luxury-boutique prices tends to land on this sweet spot

Price and value · At a starting price of about 1,700 baht a night (around 51 dollars based on deals found on booking platforms), which includes a local-style breakfast and the cafe atmosphere, it's reasonable for what you get · Consider that a boutique hotel of the same level in the Old City usually starts at 2,500–4,500 baht and up, while a hostel may be cheaper but doesn't give you this kind of privacy and design · What Live n' Leaf is really "selling" isn't just a room, but the experience of staying in a cute house in the Old City, with a host to look after you, a cafe to chill in, and a location you can walk from without hailing a ride · Prices may climb during high season (November–February) and festival periods, so it's worth comparing several platforms and booking ahead to lock in a good rate

What to know before booking · First, because there are only 5 rooms, you should book ahead, especially during high season and long weekends, as it fills up very fast · Second, if you're flying in, the property's airport transfer is convenient since the airport is close · Third, if you're driving yourself, ask about parking in advance, because it's in an Old City lane where parking can be limited, and the road is closed on Sunday nights for the Walking Street · Fourth, if you're set on the Sunday Walking Street, this location has a big edge because you can walk straight out · Fifth, ask about the details of the room you want — for example, whether it has a balcony — since each room is designed differently · Sixth, confirm the check-in/check-out times and breakfast hours with the property before you travel

The honest takeaway from real reviews · Live n' Leaf Lifestyle Homestay and Cafe is a place for people who want a cute, well-designed house in the heart of Chiang Mai's Old City, the privacy and close personal care of a homestay, plus a cafe and local-style breakfast, in a location you can actually walk from to the temples and the Walking Street, at a price that's worth it · If you understand from the start that this place sells warmth, friendliness, and location rather than big-resort facilities, you'll get a stay that fits an Old City trip perfectly · But if you want a pool, a fitness room, 5-star hotel service, or you're coming as a large family, this may not be for you, and you should pick a larger hotel in the city instead · For the right person, Live n' Leaf is a warm home that will make your Chiang Mai trip feel friendly from the very first step through the door

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Live n' Leaf Lifestyle Homestay and Cafe Chiang Mai

faq.q: Where is Live n' Leaf Lifestyle Homestay in Chiang Mai, and what's nearby?
faq.a: It's at 100 Samlan Road, Phra Singh subdistrict, in Chiang Mai's Old City, near Suan Prung Gate and Chiang Mai Gate · You can walk to Wat Phra Singh in just a few minutes, and it's close to the Sunday Walking Street, the Chiang Mai Gate market, Wat Chedi Luang, and the Three Kings Monument · Chiang Mai Airport is only 2–3 km away, about a 10 min drive

faq.q: What's the starting price at Live n' Leaf, and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about THB 1,700/night for an air-conditioned standard room (around 51 dollars based on deals found) · There are some deluxe rooms with a balcony or sitting area at a slightly higher price · There are only 5 rooms here, each designed differently, and the rate includes a local-style breakfast — it's worth comparing several platforms and booking ahead

faq.q: Who is Live n' Leaf best suited for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for couples, pairs of travelers, solo travelers, cafe lovers, and photo-takers who want to stay in a cute, well-designed house in the Old City and walk to the temples and the Walking Street · It's not ideal for large families or anyone who wants resort-style facilities like a pool or fitness room

faq.q: Does the property have breakfast and a cafe?
faq.a: Yes · The ground floor is a quiet cafe decorated in a leaf theme, and every morning there's a free local-style breakfast from about 8:00 to 10:30 AM, which many reviews praise, because you get to try genuine Northern Thai food in a warm, homey setting

faq.q: How far in advance should you book?
faq.a: Because there are only 5 rooms, during high season (Nov–Feb) and long weekends you should book several weeks ahead, as it fills up very fast · At other times, booking 1–2 weeks ahead is usually enough · Choose a free-cancellation rate first if your plans aren't certain yet

faq.q: Is there parking and an airport transfer?
faq.a: There's an airport transfer, which is convenient since the airport is only 2–3 km away (ask in advance when you book) · Parking is available but fairly limited because it's in an Old City lane · The road is closed on Sunday nights for the Walking Street, so plan your route in and out in advance
